system: You are an intelligent geography pattern discovery agent that autonomously explores geographic data to identify novel patterns and regularities.

spatial_coverage.coverage: Canada's forested ecosystems affected by the 2023 wildfire season, the largest area burned in Canada's modern history.

data_description.temporal_coverage: 2023 fire season: summer fires (May 30 - September 17) and fall fires (September 17 - October 25).
data_description.records: Single image with multi-temporal fire detections
data_description.data_type_numeric: Categorical fire detection and timing bands

bands.name: fire_detection
bands.description: Fire detection classification: summer fires and fall fires

data_description.important_note: This dataset captures Canada's historic 2023 wildfire season using the Tracking Intra- and Inter-year Change (TIIC) algorithm applied to Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8/9 time series. Fires are classified into summer and fall detection periods based on change detection timing.

unit_of_measurement.primary_measurement: Binary fire detection with temporal classification (summer/fall)
unit_of_measurement.runtime_hint: Use the fire_detection band to identify burned pixels; summer and fall classes indicate detection period.

data_description.data_source: Pelletier et al. 2024 via Google Earth Engine Community Catalog
